svg.title: Periodic patterns
svg.desc: Modern & historical tables: Modern order: atomic number. Groups link outer electrons and reactions; periods link occupied shells. Mendeleev used mass/properties, left gaps and predicted missing elements. Discoveries supported predictions; isotopes explain mass-order anomalies. Group 0: Full outer shell: 8 electrons except helium has 2. Very unreactive, monatomic gases. Boiling point increases with atomic mass down the group. Use the trend to predict values. Group 1: One outer electron → +1 ions. Li, Na, K: water → hydroxide + H₂; oxygen → oxides; chlorine → chlorides. 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Alkaline solution; reactions get more vigorous Li → Na → K. Down group: more distance/shielding → outer electron lost more easily → reactivity rises. Group 7: Seven outer electrons; gain one → −1 ions. Diatomic Cl₂, Br₂, I₂. Metal halides ionic; non-metal compounds covalent. Cl₂ green gas; Br₂ red-brown liquid; I₂ grey-black solid. Melting/boiling points rise down group. More distance/shielding → weaker attraction for incoming electron → reactivity falls. Halogen displacement: More reactive halogen displaces less reactive halogen from its aqueous salt. Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂. Ionic: Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂. Iodine cannot displace chlorine from chloride. Use group position to predict. Transition metals: Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu: generally stronger/harder/denser, higher melting and less reactive than Group 1. Many have variable ion charges, coloured compounds and catalytic uses. Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺; blue copper sulfate; iron/nickel catalysts. Trends have exceptions.
